facts.claim: Tara Lindqvist of Fjord Venture Partners wrote that it is too early for the fund right now, asked Arjun to keep her posted, and said she would be happy to look again if Nimbus Labs hits a real milestone.
Her mail asks no question and sets no date; the condition to look again is a real milestone, named in no more detail.

The investor playbook's conditional deferral says to take the conversation out of the round's count, record the condition in the investor's own words, and write when the condition is met, about that and nothing else.
The playbook holds that most passes are about timing, stage or a metric and carry a date on which they stop being true.
The playbook's passed stage treats quiet as the resting state, left alone until the condition is met.
The file's history records no earlier verdict or outcome.

inferences.claim: This is a deferral on timing with a condition, not a verdict on the company: Fjord leaves the door open and asks for nothing now.
The only note that reopens it is one about a real milestone; a routine update is the conversation she has deferred.
Fjord is out of the round's count until the condition is met.

patterns.claim: A deferral on stage or timing stops being true later, and investors who defer are often warm leads when the condition is met.
Keep me posted with nothing named commits nobody; the condition is recorded as she gave it, never filled in with a plausible one.
When the condition is met, write about that and nothing else; a routine note in between teaches the investor to skim.

hypotheses.needs: Her answer to a note about a real milestone.

hypotheses.proposition: Her request to be kept posted is a courteous close rather than an open door.
hypotheses.needs: Whether she answers anything Arjun sends.

unknowns.question: What Tara would count as a real milestone.
unknowns.relevance: She named none in particular; the note that reopens the conversation depends on it, and it must not be guessed for her.

unknowns.question: Whether Fjord wants periodic updates or only news.
unknowns.relevance: The playbook keeps on the monthly update only the investors who asked for one; being kept posted may or may not mean that.

unknowns.question: Why the fund judged it too early — stage, traction or timing.
unknowns.relevance: Each points to a different milestone and a different time to look again.

frames.primary: A conditional deferral: Fjord says it is too early and will look again on a real milestone, so the right move is to wait for one and write only then.
rivals: A soft no phrased kindly, where no milestone will reopen it.
A fund that wants regular news to track the company, where a short periodic update is welcome.

expected_vs_actual.expected: At this stage quiet is the resting state: the reason and the condition are recorded, and nothing is sent until the condition is met.
expected_vs_actual.actual: Tara deferred on timing and named a real milestone as her condition to look again; she asked for nothing more.

scenarios.do_nothing: Fjord rests as a deferred investor; nothing decays, because the conversation is parked on its condition, not live.
scenarios.act: Writing before a real milestone, with a routine update or a nudge, spends Tara's attention on the conversation she deferred and teaches her to skim the next note.
scenarios.best: Nimbus Labs hits a real milestone, Arjun writes to Tara about that alone, and she looks again with a meeting.
scenarios.worst: Routine notes wear out the open door, so when a real milestone comes she no longer reads them.

Routine updates starting to go to Tara without a new fact in them

parsed.done_when: A real milestone has gone to Tara in a note of its own, or Fjord stays parked on its condition with nothing routine sent in between.
